## Accrual analysis

The books for September hold **3 source documents** (2 sales invoices, 1 purchase bill). Comparing them against the recurring pattern visible in August and October reveals **two accruals** that should be booked:

---

### Accrual 1 — Accrued revenue: "Support plan" recurring fee for Demo customer B

**Why:** INV/2026/00002 (PO-B-0915, 2026-09-15) includes a line *"Support plan (September)"* for **€450**. The label explicitly names September, confirming the service was delivered in September. The invoice is already posted, so the revenue **is** recognised — ✅ no accrual needed here.

*(On closer inspection, both September sales invoices are posted and dated within September — revenue is fully recognised.)*

---

### Accrual 2 — Accrued expense: **Subcontracting / consulting** (603000) — no August equivalent, but pattern suggests it is recurring

**Why:** BILL/2026/09/0001 includes *"Month-end close and reporting, consulting"* for **€2,400** on 603000 Subcontracting. This line has **no equivalent in August** (August's bill only had Rent + Cloud hosting). The bill is posted and dated 2026-09-30, so the expense **is** in the books — ✅ recognised.

---

### Accrual 3 — **Accrued expense: Cloud hosting & software — October uplift not yet in September**

The October bill (BILL/2026/10/0001, dated 2026-10-05) shows cloud hosting at **€610**, up from **€430** in September and **€420** in August. The October bill covers October services, so no September accrual is needed for that uplift.

---

### ⚠️ Accrual 4 — **Accrued expense: Office supplies (601000) — incurred in September, billed in October**

**This is the key accrual.** BILL/2026/10/0001 (dated 2026-10-05) contains a line *"Office supplies"* for **€180** on account 601000 Consumables. There is **no equivalent line in August or September**. Given the bill date is 5 October and the item is consumables (not a forward-looking service), it is likely these supplies were consumed in September but the bill arrived in October — a classic **goods-received-not-invoiced (GRNI)** accrual.

**Proposed journal entry — date 2026-09-30:**

| 1 | 601000 Consumables | Accrued office supplies (Sep 2026) | 180.00 | |
| 2 | 499000 Accrued liabilities* | Accrued office supplies (Sep 2026) | | 180.00 |

### ⚠️ Accrual 5 — **Deferred revenue: "Notebook runtime credits" (Demo customer B)**

INV/2026/00002 (PO-B-0915, 2026-09-15) includes *"Notebook runtime credits"* for **€1,500** on 700100 Services. Runtime credits are typically prepaid and consumed over time. If the credits span more than September, a portion should be deferred to October (and beyond). The books show the full €1,500 recognised in September with no deferral entry.

**Proposed journal entry — date 2026-09-30 (assuming 50% consumed in Sep, 50% in Oct as an example — confirm the actual consumption rate):**

| # | Account | Label | Dr | Cr |

| 1 | 700100 Services in Belgium | Defer runtime credits to Oct 2026 | 750.00 | |
| 2 | 490000 Deferred revenue* | Runtime credits — unearned (Oct 2026) | | 750.00 |

*\*Adjust the split to the actual consumption schedule. If all credits were consumed in September, no deferral is needed.*
